meta.title: Buy PPL
meta.description: PPL is sold on a public price curve on Base. The price starts at $0.005 and rises with every purchase. The sale runs until it sells out or for 24 months, whichever comes first. Purchases are final.

hero.headline: Buy PPL on the public price curve
hero.sub: The price follows a public curve and rises as more PPL is sold. Buying earlier means a lower starting price — not a guaranteed profit.

whyPriceRises.title: Why the price rises
whyPriceRises.noManualLead: The PEOPLE team does not set or raise the price. A public formula in the sale contract sets it automatically: each purchase moves the price along the curve.
whyPriceRises.mechanism: Pricing by a public formula: price depends only on how many PPL have been sold, and anyone can check it on-chain once the contract is published.
whyPriceRises.example: From the published curve parameters: {startPrice} per PPL at the start, {midPrice} after {midSold} PPL sold (~{midRaised} raised), and {gradPrice} at graduation ({gradRaised} raised).
whyPriceRises.chartAria: PPL sale bonding curve: price versus PPL sold
whyPriceRises.contractPendingNote: The contract is not published yet. When it is, anyone will be able to check the formula on-chain.
plain: Bonding curve — a public price formula: the more PPL is sold, the higher the price.
Graduation — the moment $4M is raised: the curve closes and a public PPL pool opens.
LP tokens are locked for 24 months: nobody can withdraw the pool's money during that time.
Multisig — a wallet where several people must approve every payment.
DEX pool — an open exchange pool where anyone can trade PPL.

A lot is one purchase; the 30 days count from each purchase. Verified means you have proved once that you are a unique person (Human Passport or Telegram) — {howItWorks}. The reserve is the USDC held in the sale contract; sell-backs are paid from it.
Sell-back means you sell PPL to the reserve. Buyback means the project buys PPL with fee income. These are two different things.

curve.title: One curve, visible to everyone
curve.lead: The price is not set by hand. price = {start} × e^(k·x), where x is millions of PPL sold and k = ln(50)/100. Every figure below is computed from that formula.
curve.ceilingNote: The {ceiling} ceiling is only reached if all {supply} PPL sell. The curve closes first, at {graduation} raised.
curve.capScope: The {ceiling} cap applies during the curve sale only. After graduation the pool price is set by the free market, with no upper limit and no lower limit — the price can fall a long way, even close to zero.

whatYouGet.title: What a purchase actually gives you

items.title: PPL on your address right away
items.body: PPL is credited to your address right away, but you cannot send it to others until the full network launch. Sell-back is possible only for verified users, 30 days after each purchase.

items.title: Sell-back to the reserve
items.body: Sell-back to the reserve — verified users only. Each lot can be sold back after a 30-day hold, at the curve price at the moment you sell. Total sell-backs are capped at 2% of the reserve per day for everyone and $2,000 per person per day. Fee: 1.5%, or 3% when that day's sell-backs already exceed 1% of the reserve. Closes after graduation. Payouts in USDC on Base.

items.title: Transfers open with the full network launch
items.body: Sending PPL to other people and trading in the pool start at the full network launch, once {verified} verified participants have joined.

items.title: At {graduation} the curve closes
items.body: While the sale runs, purchase money stays in the sale reserve on Base and pays for sell-backs. At graduation {liquidityShare} goes into the public pool together with PPL at the last curve price (LP tokens locked for {lockPeriod}), and {multisigShare} goes to the project multisig, with public reporting on every spend.

timeline.title: From the curve to a free market

steps.title: The curve
steps.body: {supply} PPL on a public curve from {start} up to a {ceiling} ceiling. Anyone can buy while the sale is open: until the curve closes at {graduation} raised or {term} after opening, whichever comes first. No extensions.

steps.body: The curve stops. {liquidityShare} of the raise plus PPL at the last curve price go into a public DEX pool at exactly that price, with no jump. LP tokens are locked for {lockPeriod}. {multisigShare} goes to the project multisig with public reporting. Sell-back closes.

steps.title: Full network launch
steps.body: PPL transfers between wallets and pool trading open at the full network launch, once {verified} verified participants have joined.

steps.title: If not sold out: {term} after opening

faq.title: Questions, answered

items.a: Sell-back to the reserve — verified users only. Each lot can be sold back after a 30-day hold, at the curve price at the moment you sell. Total sell-backs are capped at 2% of the reserve per day for everyone and $2,000 per person per day. Fee: 1.5%, or 3% when that day's sell-backs already exceed 1% of the reserve. Closes after graduation. Payouts in USDC on Base.

No. It applies while the curve is running. The curve closes at {graduation} raised, around {graduationPrice} per PPL, below the cap. After graduation the pool price is set by the free market, with no upper and no lower limit — it can fall a long way, even close to zero.

items.q: Do I need the People network in my wallet?
items.a: No. The sale runs on Base only: you pay in USDC or USDT on Base. The People network is separate and is not needed to buy.

items.q: When can I send PPL to someone else?
items.a: At the full network launch, once {verified} verified participants have joined. Until then you can buy while the sale is open; selling back is limited: verified users only, 30 days after each purchase, within daily limits, until graduation.
No. All purchases are final: there are no refunds. The sale cannot be extended; unsold PPL goes to the Community Pool.

items.q: Which networks can I pay from?
items.a: On Base — in USDC or USDT. From other networks — through the built-in automatic swap (LI.FI): EVM networks (Ethereum, BNB Chain, Polygon, Arbitrum, Optimism, Avalanche and others), Tron and Solana work. TON is not supported.

faq.pumpTitle: What goes wrong on curves without a ceiling
faq.pumpLead: Bonding curves became popular through launchpads like pump.fun. These are their known problems, and what we do instead.

pumpRows.what: The price runs up without limit, so the last buyers before graduation pay many times what the first did.
pumpRows.ours: The price still rises: at graduation it is about 32 times the starting price, so late buyers pay more than early ones. The curve closes at {graduation}, around {graduationPrice}, below the {ceiling} cap.

pumpRows.what: Scripts buy in the first seconds from many wallets, then sell to real people.
pumpRows.ours: Up to {perBuy} per purchase, {perDay} per person in any 24 hours, and a {cooldown}-second pause between purchases. Per-account limits make it harder to build a large position quickly; they cannot rule out one person using several wallets.

pumpRows.what: Large holders sell everything at once and crash the price.
pumpRows.ours: Sell-back is capped at 2% of the reserve per day for everyone and $2,000 per person per day. The sell-back fee goes to the PPL buyback by the project (a separate mechanism), and pool liquidity is locked for {lockPeriod}.

pumpRows.what: A trade fills at a price much worse than the one you were shown.
pumpRows.ours: Slippage protection: if the price moves against you by more than 1% before your purchase is confirmed, the transaction is cancelled.

pumpRows.what: The token is pushed onto exchanges in the middle of the sale.
pumpRows.ours: No listings during the sale. Pool trading starts at the full network launch.

notes.text: PPL is the utility token of the People network. On the curve its price follows the published formula, and after graduation it is set by the market: it can fall as well as rise. PPL is not a security, not a share in a company, not a deposit and not an investment product, and no profit, yield or return of any kind is promised or guaranteed. Figures shown before a purchase are estimates computed from the published formula and are confirmed on-chain before you sign. Nothing on this page is investment, legal or tax advice.
Participation may be restricted or unavailable where you live, and checking the rules that apply to you is your own responsibility. Use only money you can afford to lose.

The AI-assisted reviews named above were run by the project team. They are not a security audit, and no external audit has been done yet. A bug bounty reduces risk but does not remove it: no review can prove software free of defects.
